advances: Ordinary uniform simplex transport. The conditional mean is for the stated independent-step construction.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
For $m\ge2$, condition on $J=j$ and $R=r$. The homothety from $\Delta_m$ onto $\{x\in\Delta_m:x_j\ge r\}$ has relative volume Jacobian $(1-r)^{m-1}$. The image of $\mu_m$ therefore has density $(1-r)^{-(m-1)}\mathbf 1_{\{x_j\ge r\}}$. Multiplying by the density of $R$ and integrating over $0<r<x_j$ gives $mx_j$. Averaging over $j$ gives $\sum_jx_j=1$. For $m=1$, all point laws coincide and $mx_j=1$ on the simplex.

Direct integration gives $\mathbb E R=1/(m+1)$, so independence yields $\mathbb E[X\mid W,J]=V$. Conditioning further on $(V,J)$ or on $V$ gives the two remaining identities. In particular, given $J=j$, the image of uniform probability under $w\mapsto(mw+e_j)/(m+1)$ is dominated in convex order by the probability with density $mx_j$, by conditional Jensen.
statement: For an integer $m\ge1$, let $\mu_m$ be uniform probability on $\Delta_m=\{x\in\mathbb R^m:x_j\ge0,\ \sum_jx_j=1\}$. Independently draw $W\sim\mu_m$, a uniform index $J\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and $R$ with density $m(1-r)^{m-1}$ on $(0,1)$. Write $e_j$ for the standard basis vectors. Then $X=(1-R)W+Re_J$ has law $\mu_m$. Given $J=j$, its law has density $mx_j$ relative to $\mu_m$. For $V=(mW+e_J)/(m+1)$, one has $\mathbb E[X\mid W,J]=V$ and hence $\mathbb E[X\mid V,J]=\mathbb E[X\mid V]=V$.
title: Beta-step merging on a simplex
